newsitem.title: BELGIUM: "Button-lipped" Irish fin min makes EU debut.
newsitem.headline: "Button-lipped" Irish fin min makes EU debut.

text.p: Not only will new Irish Finance Minister Charlie McCreevy not say whether the Irish punt should be revalued, he will tell you why he won't say it.

On his first visit to a European Union finance ministers meeting since taking up his post, the new man from Dublin invoked on Monday what he called alternatively the "button-lip policy" and the "McCreevy principle" -- say nothing.
"As far as I am concerned the markets will not know now or ever what I think," McCreevy told reporters. "They can make their money in their own way."

McCreevy, who said he had been studying currency markets for 30 years, was effectively not responding to questions about what the government planned to do about the punt, which is soaring within the EU's Exchange Rate Mechanism.
"The least said about these things the better," he said. "A buttoned lip is the best policy."
The McCreevy principle was, he said: "Let these people make their millions or lose their millions."
